meta.title: DSH Subagent Bridge
meta.description: Lets Codex delegate tasks to DSH as a subagent over MCP and shows running subagents in the web UI.

panel.title: DSH Subagents
panel.empty: No tasks yet. Delegate tasks from Codex via MCP and progress will show up here.
panel.connectTitle: Use DSH as a subagent in Codex
panel.usageStep1: 1. Connect Codex: send the prompt below to the DSH assistant; it registers the MCP server and adds the usage rules to the Codex instructions (~/.codex/AGENTS.md).
panel.usageStep2: 2. Open a new Codex session and state your task: all tasks run via DSH subagents while the Codex main agent decomposes, checks, and accepts.
panel.usageStep3: 3. This panel shows subagent status in real time; click a card for details (full task, result, errors).
panel.installTitle: Step one: copy the prompt and send it to the DSH assistant
panel.installHint: The current bridge URL is already embedded; the assistant handles the rest:
panel.installPrompt:
Please wire the DSH subagent bridge into Codex, endpoint: {url}
1. Register the MCP server: run codex mcp add dsh-subagent --url {url}; if codex is not on PATH, use the desktop-bundled CLI (%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\bin\<version>\codex.exe) with the same command; otherwise edit ~/.codex/config.toml and append:
[mcp_servers.dsh-subagent]
url = "{url}"
Verify with codex mcp get dsh-subagent (enabled: true).
2. Append the following usage rules to ~/.codex/AGENTS.md (create the file if missing):
## DSH subagent usage rules
- Use DSH subagents for all tasks; the main agent checks and accepts the results.
- Subagents cannot generate images: all image generation stays with the main agent.
- Write self-contained task descriptions (paths, context, acceptance criteria in task); on rejection, give concrete revision notes and delegate again.
3. When both steps are done, tell the user a new Codex session picks it up.

panel.syncNote: The DSH port changes on every start; the bridge writes the current endpoint into the Codex config (~/.codex/config.toml) at startup, so after restarting DSH you don't need to re-register — just open a new Codex session.

panel.limitsHint: Saved changes take effect immediately (no DSH restart needed). Tasks above the concurrency cap queue up; tasks past the timeout fail.
